label: CJEU C-131/12 — Google Spain (right to be forgotten)
body: 1. A search engine's indexing of personal data is "processing"; the search-engine operator is the controller for that processing.

3. The operator is obliged to remove, on request, links to pages containing personal data of the requester even where the underlying publication remains lawful — where, in light of time elapsed, the data are inadequate, irrelevant, or excessive.

4. The data subject's Charter Art. 7 + 8 rights generally override the operator's economic interest AND the public interest in finding the information — unless there is a preponderant public interest (e.g. the subject plays a role in public life).
Why it matters: Birth of the "right to be forgotten" — the precursor to GDPR Art. 17. Establishes the public-interest balancing for delisting.
